newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Heavy develops first Japanese helicopter.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Heavy develops first Japanese helicopter.

text.p: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd (MHI) said on Friday it had developed the first helicopter using Japanese technology for both the body and engine of the aircraft.
The MH2000, a seven to 12-seater medium-sized helicopter, was developed as a multi-purpose helicopter capable of business flights, rescue missions and emergency transportation.
It has been certified by Japan's Transport Ministry.
MHI plans to accept orders for the helicopter, to be priced at about 400 million yen, in the autumn and hopes to sell 100 in Japan over the next 10 years, a company spokesman said.
MHI wants to sell the helicopter in Southeast Asia sometime in the future, he said.
Kawasaki Heavy is the only Japanese company producing helicopters for commercial use. Kawasaki's helicopters are under the licence of Germany's Messerschmit.
Kawasaki Heavy, Fuji Heavy and MHI produce helicopters for the military under foreign makers' licences.
